description: Pane Carasau is a traditional flatbread from the sunny island of Sardinia. This century-old recipe was originally used by shepherds so that they could take bread with them during the many months away from home but has now become a mainstream item in modern Sardinian cuisine. Sardinian bakeries pride themselves with making this crisp bread as thin as possible and our Pane Carasau is as thin as it comes. Grill it on a BBQ or a grille for a few seconds (until it starts turning darker) then stack it on a platter drizzling EVOO and a pinch of salt between each layer. You will not believe how popular this bread is at family gatherings or dinners with friends. Exceptional with a fresh Sardinian Pecorino Cheese, seafood platters, or just as a healthy, tasty, snack. The Battacone artisan bakery was born in the far 1975 in Irgoli, in the heart of the Barony. Of the traditions of our territory we have treasured, transferring them to the production of the typical bread of Sardinia, the Pane Carasau, known beyond the Tyrrhenian Sea as music paper. With the same passion and the same recipe of our ancestors, today we can let you taste the taste of the bread that was made at home many years ago. Over time, the quality of the products and all their characteristics have remained intact, but modern means have enabled us to achieve important results. Today the Battacone bakery is able to meet the needs of all its customers throughout the country, guaranteeing quality and professionalism. In any part of Italy it is possible to have our products. If you want to have an important showcase of our products in your store, and let you know one of the most typical and good traditional Sardinian recipes, all you have to do is contact us and we will be at your disposal to meet your needs.

bullet_point: [2 Envelopes - 250 gr each - total 0.5 kg (17.6 us oz), A crispy sheet of durum wheat meal bread, Ideal for Cheese Starters - Product of Italy, Once opened, make sure you seal the package properly]
description:
A crispy sheet of durum wheat meal bread
The sheets of bread are removed from the oven piping hot and bulging, then are separated by hand and placed back in the oven to make them fragrant and crisp.

Light bread with the fragrance of wheat
Matched with tangy or mild cheese spreads, cold cuts and cheeses, ideal for tasty snacks to enliven your cocktail hour.

This ancient bread was made for the shepherds who spent long solitary months away from the village, and needed easy-to-carry, long-lasting food. Making the Sardinian Pane Carasau was traditionally a female art, involving the use of special durum wheat flours and other selected ingredients, long hours kneading the dough and an oven at just the right temperature. The end result is a crisp, fragrant bread, straw yellow in colour with slight brown tinges. Its crisp, thin sheets and intense flavour make it perfect for both simple and special dishes. One of the most common ways of eating Pane Carasau consists in damping it in cold water, thus making it soft enough to fold round cheeses, cold cuts or cheese spreads.

Pane Carasau (Sardinian Carasau bread) is a millennial tradition which combines the sun, the land and the grain with the wise mankind's work, the flour and the clear spring waters. Well-known with the name "Carta da Musica" ("Music sheets"), the thin sheets of Carasau bread are an ideal companion for pork products, cheeses and fish starters. The origin of baking, including the Sardinian bread-making, goes back thousands of years, and it has always been the principal element of human nutrition. The process of baking (grain, water, salt and yeast) is different depending on the use of the bread. The Carasau bread is originating from Nuoro: the shepherds used to spend long periods alone in the fold, in the countryside, far away from home, so they needed a type of bread that could last longer.

description: Handmade Pizza Taralli Crackers Giannetti Artisans’s Pizza Taralli Crackers from Puglia (Apulia) are a remarkable handmade product. In case you don’t know what taralli are, here is a bit of a background: Taralli are toroidal Italian snack food, common all over the southern half of the Italian Peninsula. Taralli are tasty crackers similar in texture to a breadstick or pretzel. In fact, taralli are both sweet and sugar-glazed or savory. With this being said, savory taralli are usually flavored with onion, garlic, poppy seeds, fennel, pepper, chili or just salt. In fact Giannetti Artisans sourced a small family run business in Bari who makes our taralli crackers with a secret family recipe. To this day, they have never revealed their recipe! Furthermore, the Extra Virgin Olive Oil used in the taralli crackers is from an area called Bitonto, known as the Olive Oil capital of Puglia (Apulia). Not to mention the fact that the producer uses flour that comes from the Apulia area called “Tavoniere delle Puglie”. It is the second largest wheat producer in Italy right after Padania. The Apulia region is well-known for their baking abilities and high quality wheat products. If you take a close look at the shape of the crackers, you can tell they are truly handmade. By all means, crunch in and try for yourself! – (300 gr) 10.58 oz bag. Ingredients: Wheat Flour “00”, Olive Oil, Extra Virgin Olive Oil, Brewer’s Yeast, White Wine, Salt. (contains sulfates).

description: Simit, gevrek, bokegh, or koulouri is a circular bread, typically encrusted with sesame seeds or, less commonly, poppy, flax or sunflower seeds, found across the cuisines of the former Ottoman Empire, and the Middle East. Simit's size, crunch, chewiness, and other characteristics vary slightly by region. The bagel, dating back 600 years ago, was called the “Sultan’s gift” as a special food that the Ottoman sultans presented to the soldiers after their iftar meals. The simit, which was first produced in Istanbul in 1525 and located in the palace kitchen, has become a traditional food of the people, rather than becoming a palace pastry. According to the court records of Üsküdar at that time, the bagel, which was known to have been standardized for the first time in 1593, spreads to other countries thanks to the Ottoman Empire. One of the traveler Evliya Çelebi writes that there were 70 bagel bakeries in Istanbul in the 1630s. Hekim Bereket’s manuscript is mentioned in the Turkish medical book (Tufet-i Mubariz). In the oil painting where painter Jean Brindesi painted Istanbul of the 19th century, the bagel sellers on the streets draw attention. Painter Warwick Goble’s oil painting “Simit Vendor” describes a donut vendor in Istanbul in 1906. II. The bagel, which was forbidden for a while due to the famine during the World War period, regains its place in daily life when flour production reaches a normal level. 1 sesame bagel (simit) is 110-120 gram (0.24-027lb) 100 gr Sesame Bagel Calorie 272 kcal

On long voyages Baltic sailors fill the holds of their ships with it- sourdough rye lasts for months. Latvians soak rye bread in milk and eggs to make bread pudding. They serve rye bread croutons fried in garlic and butter as bar snacks. Like rice in Asia, rye bread -- known as rupjmaize in Latvian -- is considered holy. It is never wasted. To leave it bottom side up on the counter is considered disrespectful. -The bread itself -- dense, dark, sweet/sour with a hint of caraway -- marries perfectly with the foods of Baltic farms and fisheries: rich butter, herring, smoked meats, fish, and pork sausage. -While the rye breads of Denmark and Sweden are known as the base for those countries excellent open-faced sandwiches, Latvian rye bread, made without any wheat, is considered the ne plus ultra of rye breads. -For decades bread lovers hungering for 100 percent sour dough rye have had to air freight it from Europe at high cost. Now, thanks to Black Rooster Food, you can buy it, made in USA..

title: Sean Brocks Jimmy Red Cornbread Mix
bullet_point: [Acclaimed chef Sean Brock's Jimmy Red Cornbread Mix is a living testament to the history of heirloom crops of the South Carolina Lowcountry, Jimmy Red Corn, once almost extinct, has been preserved for centuries through seed saving, and is now masterfully harvested by Geechie Boy Mill., Gluten Free, Heirloom, and Non-GMO, Net Weight 16 OZ (453 Grams)]
description:
A MESSAGE FROM CHEF SEAN BROCK

What you are holding in your hands is a very important piece of Southern food history. Over a decade ago, Jimmy Red corn was nearly extinct. Thanks to a dedicated community of farmers and many, many years of seed saving, this corn is back and better than ever. It makes the best cornbread I have ever had and I'm thrilled to finally be able to share it with you. So fire up your skillet, invite some loved ones, and help keep this special piece of living food history alive.

JIMMY RED CORNBREAD RECIPE
Makes one 10-inch round loaf

1 package Jimmy Red Cornbread Mix
2-1/2 cups Full Fat Buttermilk
2 Each Whole Eggs
1/2 cup + 4 Tbsp Lard, melted (or grapeseed oil, butter or vegetable shortening)
A pinch of black pepper & a pinch of coarse salt

Preheat the oven to 450°F. Put a 10-inch cast iron skillet in the oven for at least 10 minutes.

Combine the cornbread mix with the black pepper, buttermilk, and eggs. Stir in the melted lard. Move the skillet from the oven to the stove, placing it over high heat. Add half of the remaining lard and swirl to coat the skillet. Pour in the batter, distributing it evenly. It should sizzle.

Transfer back to the oven and bake the cornbread for about 20 minutes until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean. Brush the top with the last of the lard and sprinkle with the coarse salt. Serve warm, directly from the skillet.

description: Simit, gevrek, bokegh, or koulouri is a circular bread, typically encrusted with sesame seeds or, less commonly, poppy, flax or sunflower seeds, found across the cuisines of the former Ottoman Empire, and the Middle East. Simit's size, crunch, chewiness, and other characteristics vary slightly by region. The bagel, dating back 600 years ago, was called the “Sultan’s gift” as a special food that the Ottoman sultans presented to the soldiers after their iftar meals. The simit, which was first produced in Istanbul in 1525 and located in the palace kitchen, has become a traditional food of the people, rather than becoming a palace pastry. According to the court records of Üsküdar at that time, the bagel, which was known to have been standardized for the first time in 1593, spreads to other countries thanks to the Ottoman Empire. One of the traveler Evliya Çelebi writes that there were 70 bagel bakeries in Istanbul in the 1630s. Hekim Bereket’s manuscript is mentioned in the Turkish medical book (Tufet-i Mubariz). In the oil painting where painter Jean Brindesi painted Istanbul of the 19th century, the bagel sellers on the streets draw attention. Painter Warwick Goble’s oil painting “Simit Vendor” describes a donut vendor in Istanbul in 1906. II. The bagel, which was forbidden for a while due to the famine during the World War period, regains its place in daily life when flour production reaches a normal level. 1 sesame bagel (simit) is 110-120 gram (0.24-027lb) 100 gr Sesame Bagel Calorie 272 kcal

description: Pane Carasau is a traditional flatbread from the sunny island of Sardinia. This century-old recipe was originally used by shepherds so that they could take bread with them during the many months away from home but has now become a mainstream item in modern Sardinian cuisine. Sardinian bakeries pride themselves with making this crisp bread as thin as possible and our Pane Carasau is as thin as it comes. Grill it on a BBQ or a grille for a few seconds (until it starts turning darker) then stack it on a platter drizzling EVOO and a pinch of salt between each layer. You will not believe how popular this bread is at family gatherings or dinners with friends. Exceptional with a fresh Sardinian Pecorino Cheese, seafood platters, or just as a healthy, tasty, snack. The Battacone artisan bakery was born in the far 1975 in Irgoli, in the heart of the Barony. Of the traditions of our territory we have treasured, transferring them to the production of the typical bread of Sardinia, the Pane Carasau, known beyond the Tyrrhenian Sea as music paper. With the same passion and the same recipe of our ancestors, today we can let you taste the taste of the bread that was made at home many years ago. Over time, the quality of the products and all their characteristics have remained intact, but modern means have enabled us to achieve important results. Today the Battacone bakery is able to meet the needs of all its customers throughout the country, guaranteeing quality and professionalism. In any part of Italy it is possible to have our products. If you want to have an important showcase of our products in your store, and let you know one of the most typical and good traditional Sardinian recipes, all you have to do is contact us and we will be at your disposal to meet your needs.

Back home with his family at their adobe house in Ventura, California, Emilio planted the chile seeds. Those chiles grew extremely well in the temperature climate of Ventura. Soon Emilio had so many chiles he had to give them away. Everyone loved them! That's when he knew he had something special. In 2003, B&G Foods purchased the Ortega brand. The bagel, dating back 600 years ago, was called the “Sultan’s gift” as a special food that the Ottoman sultans presented to the soldiers after their iftar meals. The simit, which was first produced in Istanbul in 1525 and located in the palace kitchen, has become a traditional food of the people, rather than becoming a palace pastry. According to the court records of Üsküdar at that time, the bagel, which was known to have been standardized for the first time in 1593, spreads to other countries thanks to the Ottoman Empire. One of the traveler Evliya Çelebi writes that there were 70 bagel bakeries in Istanbul in the 1630s. Hekim Bereket’s manuscript is mentioned in the Turkish medical book (Tufet-i Mubariz). In the oil painting where painter Jean Brindesi painted Istanbul of the 19th century, the bagel sellers on the streets draw attention. Painter Warwick Goble’s oil painting “Simit Vendor” describes a donut vendor in Istanbul in 1906. II. description: -All the countries that hug the Baltic Sea bake bread using rye flour -- rye is indigenous to the region. But it is Latvia, on the eastern shore of the Baltic sea, that produces the most delicious highest quality rye bread, as evidenced by top prizes at food exhibitions and by exports to neighboring countries. -Latvian rye bread has been praised in Gourmet magazine by its former editor-in-chief Ruth Reichl: “This is powerful stuff that reminds you of why bread is called the staff of life. I am pretty sure you could live on it alone...” -One hundred percent sourdough rye bread is the traditional staple of Latvia, and it is central to Latvian culinary and cultural history. For a thousand years Latvians baked this bread in wood burning ovens reaching 1800 degrees fahrenheit, using 100 percent rye flour, sourdough starter, a hint of caraway and little else. -In Latvia babies teethe on the rye bread. On long voyages Baltic sailors fill the holds of their ships with it- sourdough rye lasts for months. Latvians soak rye bread in milk and eggs to make bread pudding. They serve rye bread croutons fried in garlic and butter as bar snacks. Like rice in Asia, rye bread -- known as rupjmaize in Latvian -- is considered holy. It is never wasted. To leave it bottom side up on the counter is considered disrespectful. -The bread itself -- dense, dark, sweet/sour with a hint of caraway -- marries perfectly with the foods of Baltic farms and fisheries: rich butter, herring, smoked meats, fish, and pork sausage. -While the rye breads of Denmark and Sweden are known as the base for those countries excellent open-faced sandwiches, Latvian rye bread, made without any wheat, is considered the ne plus ultra of rye breads. -For decades bread lovers hungering for 100 percent sour dough rye have had to air freight it from Europe at high cost. Now, thanks to Black Rooster Food, you can buy it, made in USA..

description:
The 150 year Ortega tradition all started with Maria Conception Jacinta Dominguez Ortega, or as we like to call her, Mama. Mama Ortega. Mama's memorable cooking did more than just bring her family together. It was in Mama's kitchen that her 11th child, Emilio, established the Ortega Chile Packing Company. Emilio's fascination with chiles began when he moved to New Mexico in 1890. Here he encountered the state's popular big red chiles. When he returned home to California a few years later, he brought with him chile pepper seeds and many recipes for dishes he had grown to love while in New Mexico. Back home with his family at their adobe house in Ventura, California, Emilio planted the chile seeds. Those chiles grew extremely well in the temperature climate of Ventura. Soon Emilio had so many chiles he had to give them away. Everyone loved them! That's when he knew he had something special. In 2003, B&G Foods purchased the Ortega brand. Like Emilio Ortega, B&G Foods has a long tradition of commitment to quality. So today, when a family picks up a can of chiles or a box of taco shells, they know they are getting the very best. This web site has been created to continue the rich heritage of the Ortega family. By sharing our collection of delicious Mexican recipes, we hope to help you create fond memories of great meals shared with your family.

Fue en la cocina de mamá donde su 11º hijo, Emilio, estableció la Compañía de Embalaje Ortega Chile. La fascinación de Emilio por los chiles comenzó cuando se mudó a Nuevo México en 1890. מסורת Ortega 150 שנה החלה הכל עם מריה קונספט ג'סינטה דומינגז אורטגה, או כפי שאנחנו אוהבים לקרוא לה, אמא. Mama Ortega. הבישול הבלתי נשכח של אמא עשה יותר מאשר רק להביא את המשפחה שלה יחד. במטבח של אמא הוא היה הילד ה-11 שלה, אמיליו, הקימה את חברת האריזה של אורטגה צ'ילה. הקסם של אמיליה עם צ'ילס החלה כאשר עבר לניו מקסיקו בשנת 1890. כאן הוא נתקל בצ'ילים האדומים הגדולים הפופולריים של המדינה. כשהוא חזר הביתה לקליפורניה כמה שנים לאחר מכן, הוא הביא איתו זרעי פלפל צ'ילה ומתכונים רבים למנות שהוא גדל לאהוב בזמן בניו מקסיקו. חזרה הביתה עם משפחתו בבית האדובי שלהם בוונטורה, קליפורניה, אמיליו שתלה את זרעי הצ'ילה. הצ'ילים האלה גדלו היטב באקלים הטמפרטורה של ונטורה. עד מהרה היו אמיליו כל כך הרבה צ'ילים שהוא היה צריך לתת אותם. כולם אהבו אותם! ואז הוא ידע שיש לו משהו מיוחד. בשנת 2003, B&G Foods רכשו את המותג Ortega. כמו אמיליו אורטגה, ל-B&G Foods יש מסורת ארוכה של מחויבות לאיכות. אז היום, כשמשפחה אוספת פחית של צ'ילים או קופסה של צדפי טאקו הם יודעים שהם מקבלים את הטוב ביותר. אתר אינטרנט זה נוצר כדי להמשיך את המורשת העשירה של משפחת Ortega. על ידי שיתוף אוסף המתכונים המקסיקניים הטעימים שלנו, אנו מקווים לעזור לכם ליצור זיכרונות אהובים של ארוחות נהדרות המשותפות עם המשפחה שלכם.

Mama Ortega. لقد أدى طهي الأم الذي لا يُنسى أكثر من مجرد أن تجمع عائلتها. كان في مطبخ الأم أن طفلها الحادي عشر، إيميليو، أسست شركة أورتيغا شيلي. بدأ تعشق إميلو مع تشيلس عندما انتقله إلى نيو مكسيكو في عام 1890. لقد واجه هنا شيلز الأحمر الكبير الشائع في الدولة. عندما عاد إلى المنزل إلى كاليفورنيا بعد بضع سنوات، أحضر معه بذور الفلفل الحار والعديد من الوصفات للأطباق التي نمت لتحبها بينما في نيو المكسيك. العودة إلى المنزل مع عائلته في منزلهم الأدوبي في فينتورا، كاليفورنيا، وزرع إيميليو بذور التشيل. نمت هذه الملابس بشكل جيد للغاية في درجة حرارة فينتورا. وقريبًا كان لدى اميليو الكثير من الأشياء التي كان عليهم أن يعطيها. سيحبها الجميع! هذا عندما عرف أنه يمتلك شيئًا مميزًا. في عام 2003، اشترت بي آند جي فودز العلامة التجارية أورتيجا. مثل إميليو أورتيجا، فإن بي آند جي فودز لديه تقليد طويل يتمثل في الالتزام بالجودة. لذا اليوم، عندما تلتقط العائلة علبة من تشيل أو صندوق من أصداف التاكو، فإنها تعلم أنها تحصل على الأفضل. تم إنشاء هذا الموقع الإلكتروني لاستمرار التراث الغني لعائلة أورتيغا. من خلال مشاركة مجموعتنا من الوصفات المكسيكية اللذيذة، نأمل أن نساعدك على خلق ذكريات موسعة من الوجبات الرائعة المشتركة مع عائلتك.

A tradição Ortega de 150 anos começou com Maria Conception Jacinta Dominguez Ortega, ou como gostamos de chamá-la, Mamãe. Mamãe Ortega. A culinária memorável da mamãe fez mais do que apenas unir sua família. Foi na cozinha da mamãe que seu décimo primeiro filho, Emilio, estabeleceu a Ortega Chile. A fascinação de Emilio por chiles começou quando se mudou para o Novo México em 1890. Aqui, ele encontrou as populares pimentas vermelhas do estado. Quando voltou para casa à Califórnia alguns anos depois, ele trouxe com ele sementes de pimenta do chile e muitas receitas de pratos que ele cresceu para amar durante o Novo México. De volta para casa com sua família em sua casa adobe em Ventura, Califórnia, Emilio plantou as sementes do Chile. Aquelas chiles cresceram extremamente bem no clima de temperatura de Ventura. Logo, Emilio tinha tantas chilas que tinha de entregá-las. Todos os adoram! Foi quando ele sabia que tinha algo especial. Em 2003, a B&G Foods adquiriu a marca Ortega. Como Emilio Ortega, a B&G Foods tem uma longa tradição de compromisso com a qualidade. Então, hoje, quando uma família pega uma lata de chiles ou uma caixa de taco, ela sabe que está recebendo o melhor. Este site foi criado para continuar a rica herança da família Ortega. Compartilhando nossa coleção de deliciosas receitas mexicanas, esperamos ajudar você a criar lembranças de ótimas refeições compartilhadas com sua família.

150 年的 Ortega 传统都始于 Maria Conception Jacinta Dominguez Ortega ,或者我们喜欢称之为她妈妈。 Mama Ortega。 Mama 令人难忘的烹饪不仅仅是把她的家人聚在一起。 在妈妈的厨房里,她的第 11 个孩子Emilio 成立了 Ortega Chile 包装公司。 Emilio 于 1890 年搬到新墨西哥时,开始对智利的着迷。 在这里,他遇到了州流行的红辣椒。 几年后回到加利福尼亚州时,他带着辣椒籽和许多食谱,在新墨西哥州长大喜爱的菜肴。 Emilio 在加利福尼亚州文图拉的土豆屋与家人一起回家。 这些智利在文图拉的气候下生长非常好。 不久,Emilio 有这么多的智利,他不得不把他们丢掉。 人见人爱的! 当他知道他有一些特别的事情。 2003 年,B&G Foods 购买了 Ortega 品牌。 与 Emilio Ortega 一样,B&G Foods 一直秉持对质量的承诺。 今天,当一个家庭拿起一罐辣椒或一盒玉米饼时,他们知道他们得到的是最好的。 这个网站旨在延续 Ortega 家族的丰富传统。 通过分享我们收集的美味墨西哥食谱,我们希望帮助您创造与家人分享美好膳食的回忆。

這 150 年的奧爾特加傳統始於瑪麗亞受孕 Jacinta Dominguez Ortega,或者我們喜歡稱她為媽媽。 Mama Ortega。 媽媽令人難忘的烹飪不僅僅是將她的家人聚在一起。 正是在媽媽的廚房裡,她的第11個孩子 Emilio 創立了 Ortega Chile 包裝公司。 Emilio 自 1890 年搬到新墨西哥時,對智利的迷惑開始。 在這裡,他遇到了該州熱門的大紅智利。 幾年後,他回到加州時,他帶來了辣椒籽和許多食譜,供他在新墨西哥州時所喜愛的菜餚。 Emilio 與家人一起回到家,在加州文圖拉的adobe house種植了辣椒種子。 這些智利在 Ventura 的溫度氣候中生長非常好。 不久,Emilio 就有這麼多智利人,他不得不放棄。 每個人都喜歡它們! 他就知道自己有一些特別的東西。 2003 年,B&G Foods 購買了 Ortega 品牌。 與 Emilio Ortega一樣,B&G Foods 對品質有長期承諾。 所以今天,當一家人拿起一罐智利或一盒玉米餅,他們知道自己正在得到最好的。 本網站旨在延續 Ortega 家族豐富的傳統。 透過分享我們的美味墨西哥食譜系列,我們希望幫助您與家人共享的美味餐點創造美好的回憶。

150년 Ortega의 전통은 모두 Maria Conception Jacinta Dominguez Ortega로 시작되었거나 엄마라고 부르고 싶어합니다. Mama Ortega. 엄마의 기억에 남는 요리는 단지 가족을 모으는 것 이상을 했습니다. 엄마의 부엌에서 11번째 아이인 에밀리오가 칠레 오르테가 패킹 회사를 설립했습니다. 칠레에 대한 에밀리오의 매력은 1890년 뉴 멕시코로 이주했을 때 시작되었습니다. 여기서 그는 주에서 인기 있는 큰 빨간 칠을 만났습니다. 몇 년 후 캘리포니아로 집으로 돌아왔을 때, 그는 칠레 후추 씨앗과 뉴 멕시코에서 사랑하기 위해 자랐던 많은 요리법을 가져왔습니다. 에밀리오 캘리포니아의 벤츄라에 있는 어도비 하우스에서 가족과 함께 집으로 돌아가 칠레 씨앗을 심었습니다. 이 칠레는 Ventura의 온도 기후에서 매우 잘 자랐습니다. 곧 에밀리오가 그들에게 줄 수 있는 많은 칠레를 가지고 있었습니다. 모두가 좋아했습니다! 그가 특별한 것을 가지고 있다는 것을 알았을 때입니다. 2003년, B&G Foods는 Ortega 브랜드를 구입했습니다. Emilio Ortega와 마찬가지로 B&G Foods는 품질에 대한 오랜 헌신의 전통을 가지고 있습니다. 그래서 오늘날 가족이 칠레 캔이나 타코 껍질 상자를 집어들면 그들은 최고의 것을 얻고 있다는 것을 알고 있습니다. 이 웹 사이트는 Ortega 가문의 풍부한 유산을 계속하기 위해 만들어졌습니다. 맛있는 멕시코 레시피 컬렉션을 공유함으로써, 가족과 함께 나누는 훌륭한 식사에 대한 추억을 만드는 데 도움을 드리기를 바랍니다.

In the 1930's, Taichiro Morinaga was trying to create a new kind of chewing gum for Japan. Back then, it was very impolite to take food out of your mouth. So Mr. Morinaga tried to create a more culturally accepted version of chewing gum- one that could be swallowed. Fortunately, Mr. Morinaga already made outstanding caramel with a uniquely chewy, creamy texture. It was unlike anything else in Japan. In 1931, he added natural strawberry flavor to his caramel recipe and Chewlets was born. Then in 1975, after decades of hard work perfecting his recipe, Mr. Morinaga re-introduced Chewlets to Japan as the wonderful candy we now know as HI-CHEW. Since then, HI-CHEW has been produced in over 113 flavors and has become the most popular chewy candy in Japan. Today. It's rapidly becoming an American favorite. description: The 150 year Ortega tradition all started with Maria Conception Jacinta Dominguez Ortega, or as we like to call her, Mama. Mama Ortega. Mama's memorable cooking did more than just bring her family together. It was in Mama's kitchen that her 11th child, Emilio, established the Ortega Chile Packing Company. Emilio's fascination with chiles began when he moved to New Mexico in 1890. Here he encountered the state's popular big red chiles. When he returned home to California a few years later, he brought with him chile pepper seeds and many recipes for dishes he had grown to love while in New Mexico. Back home with his family at their adobe house in Ventura, California, Emilio planted the chile seeds. Those chiles grew extremely well in the temperature climate of Ventura. Soon Emilio had so many chiles he had to give them away. Everyone loved them! That's when he knew he had something special. In 2003, B&G Foods purchased the Ortega brand. Like Emilio Ortega, B&G Foods has a long tradition of commitment to quality. So today, when a family picks up a can of chiles or a box of taco shells, they know they are getting the very best. This web site has been created to continue the rich heritage of the Ortega family. description: Simit, gevrek, bokegh, or koulouri is a circular bread, typically encrusted with sesame seeds or, less commonly, poppy, flax or sunflower seeds, found across the cuisines of the former Ottoman Empire, and the Middle East. Simit's size, crunch, chewiness, and other characteristics vary slightly by region. The bagel, dating back 600 years ago, was called the “Sultan’s gift” as a special food that the Ottoman sultans presented to the soldiers after their iftar meals. The simit, which was first produced in Istanbul in 1525 and located in the palace kitchen, has become a traditional food of the people, rather than becoming a palace pastry. According to the court records of Üsküdar at that time, the bagel, which was known to have been standardized for the first time in 1593, spreads to other countries thanks to the Ottoman Empire. One of the traveler Evliya Çelebi writes that there were 70 bagel bakeries in Istanbul in the 1630s. Hekim Bereket’s manuscript is mentioned in the Turkish medical book (Tufet-i Mubariz). In the oil painting where painter Jean Brindesi painted Istanbul of the 19th century, the bagel sellers on the streets draw attention. Painter Warwick Goble’s oil painting “Simit Vendor” describes a donut vendor in Istanbul in 1906. II. The bagel, which was forbidden for a while due to the famine during the World War period, regains its place in daily life when flour production reaches a normal level. 1 sesame bagel (simit) is 110-120 gram (0.24-027lb) 100 gr Sesame Bagel Calorie 272 kcal

description: We've been getting a lot of orders since March First and the covid19 panic started to set in. Not really sure why but we are and we thank everyone for trying our bread and other products. The bread that we make is unique in that not only do we not use flour - we don't add anything other than a bit of sea salt. We start with organic grain that we buy locally - two farms and both are within a thirty minute drive from our bakery. We then soak, rinse and clean the grain then let it sprout, grind it into a mash or what we call a "proto dough" to which we add our sprouted natural leaven or sourdough and just a bit of salt. That's it. That's the formulae. We DO NOT add preservatives so if you order our bread, we want to get it to you as quickly as possible. We bake on Tuesday and Friday night shipping on Wednesday and Saturday. Most of the orders we ship on Wednesday are to area customers - Northeastern states USA. Saturday's bake is when we usually ship to California, Florida, Texas and elsewhere. No hard rule on this - especially if Monday following saturday is a holiday in which case we may not ship at all. To try to protect your bread, we will vacuum seal the bread in a plastic bag. When you get the bread or pita, we recommend taking it out of the vacuum seal bag and then storing it in the freezer in the freezer bag we provide. We are developing a beeswax wrap for our loaves and we hope to have that as an available option before summer gets here. We want to eliminate plastic packaging and have done so with our flax granola. description:
How to make delicious Takoyaki

1.Takoyaki flour, water510cc（17.25 fluid ounce), and eggs in a bowl to make batter with a whisk

2.Thickness of the batter should be like potage soup.

3.Warm the takoyaki grill pan at 200℃(392°F)

4.Grease oil inside cups of a takoyaki grill pan by oil brush.

5.Pour batter into the cups to the full.

6.Put octopus, red ginger, and green onion , tempura flakes ,in each hole.

7.When batter Lower half become rounds and brown,Turn the takoyaki balls turning with a Takoyaki pick.

8.Keep turning them over until they are round and brown all over.

9.When balls become rounds and brown, remove them from the pan and place in a plate.

10.Put sauce and mayonnaise on takoyaki balls and sprinkle bonito flakes and aonori(seaweed powder) on the top.

Painter Warwick Goble’s oil painting “Simit Vendor” describes a donut vendor in Istanbul in 1906. II. description: Pane Carasau is a traditional flatbread from the sunny island of Sardinia. This century-old recipe was originally used by shepherds so that they could take bread with them during the many months away from home but has now become a mainstream item in modern Sardinian cuisine. Sardinian bakeries pride themselves with making this crisp bread as thin as possible and our Pane Carasau is as thin as it comes. Grill it on a BBQ or a grille for a few seconds (until it starts turning darker) then stack it on a platter drizzling EVOO and a pinch of salt between each layer. You will not believe how popular this bread is at family gatherings or dinners with friends. Exceptional with a fresh Sardinian Pecorino Cheese, seafood platters, or just as a healthy, tasty, snack. The Battacone artisan bakery was born in the far 1975 in Irgoli, in the heart of the Barony. Of the traditions of our territory we have treasured, transferring them to the production of the typical bread of Sardinia, the Pane Carasau, known beyond the Tyrrhenian Sea as music paper. With the same passion and the same recipe of our ancestors, today we can let you taste the taste of the bread that was made at home many years ago. Over time, the quality of the products and all their characteristics have remained intact, but modern means have enabled us to achieve important results. Today the Battacone bakery is able to meet the needs of all its customers throughout the country, guaranteeing quality and professionalism. In any part of Italy it is possible to have our products. If you want to have an important showcase of our products in your store, and let you know one of the most typical and good traditional Sardinian recipes, all you have to do is contact us and we will be at your disposal to meet your needs.

description: -All the countries that hug the Baltic Sea bake bread using rye flour -- rye is indigenous to the region. But it is Latvia, on the eastern shore of the Baltic sea, that produces the most delicious highest quality rye bread, as evidenced by top prizes at food exhibitions and by exports to neighboring countries. -Latvian rye bread has been praised in Gourmet magazine by its former editor-in-chief Ruth Reichl: “This is powerful stuff that reminds you of why bread is called the staff of life. I am pretty sure you could live on it alone...” -One hundred percent sourdough rye bread is the traditional staple of Latvia, and it is central to Latvian culinary and cultural history. For a thousand years Latvians baked this bread in wood burning ovens reaching 1800 degrees fahrenheit, using 100 percent rye flour, sourdough starter, a hint of caraway and little else. -In Latvia babies teethe on the rye bread. On long voyages Baltic sailors fill the holds of their ships with it- sourdough rye lasts for months. Latvians soak rye bread in milk and eggs to make bread pudding. They serve rye bread croutons fried in garlic and butter as bar snacks. Like rice in Asia, rye bread -- known as rupjmaize in Latvian -- is considered holy. It is never wasted. To leave it bottom side up on the counter is considered disrespectful. -The bread itself -- dense, dark, sweet/sour with a hint of caraway -- marries perfectly with the foods of Baltic farms and fisheries: rich butter, herring, smoked meats, fish, and pork sausage. -While the rye breads of Denmark and Sweden are known as the base for those countries excellent open-faced sandwiches, Latvian rye bread, made without any wheat, is considered the ne plus ultra of rye breads. -For decades bread lovers hungering for 100 percent sour dough rye have had to air freight it from Europe at high cost. How to Freeze Our Tortillas: Do you have extra tortillas that you want to save for a later date? Keep reading to see how to best freeze our tortillas. If the product is unopened, leave it that way. If you’ve already opened the package, leave the product in the package, press out any additional air, and seal well. Our packaging is not designed for freezing, so to protect the package, we recommend placing the package inside of a freezer safe zip-lock bag. Lay the tortillas down flat in your freezer. Moving back and forth between frozen, to thawed, and then frozen again, may negatively impact the texture of the tortilla. 24 hours before you’re ready to use the tortillas, move the package, or amount of tortillas you plan to use, from the freezer to the refrigerator. Gradually thaw the tortillas out rather than shocking them from the freezer to room temperature. 30 minutes before use, place the package at room temperature. Do not place the frozen tortillas in a microwave to thaw out quickly, as it may cause the tortillas to stick together and become brittle.

title: Italian Mario Fongo Mini Rubata Breadsticks, 3.53oz (100g), Pack of 4
bullet_point: [Made With Organic Extra Virgin Olive Oil, Hand Rolled, natural leavening, 100% Italian Crackers, Perfect Snack Size Bag]
description: Just as good as when they were first baked in 1679, Mario Fongo's Rubata delight the palate with their delicate flavour and compact texture, making them ideal for the most imaginative combos. The rubata, traditional right down to its name, which means "fallen" in the local Piedmont dialect, is a bread-stick made by rolling over the sheet of dough so that it takes on a very dense consistency. Mario Fongo's rubata vary in length from fifteen to thirty centimetres and have a distinctive knobbly appearance. The rubata is the oldest form of bread-stick: the story goes that it was baked for the first time in 1679 at the Savoy court, when the court baker, Antonio Brunero, following the instructions of the physician, Teobaldo Pecchio, devised this recipe to nourish the future Vittorio Amedeo II, who was sickly and unable to digest any bread, apart from the crust. This product met with an immediate and fortunate success, so much so that one of its better-known enthusiasts was Napoleon Bonaparte, who had even organized a courier service to transport what he called les petits bactons de Turin from Turin to Paris and rubata bread-sticks continue to meet with great appreciation today, both in Italy and worldwide. For years now, Mario Fongo has been producing his rubata, with masterly care and today, this classic of Piedmont cuisine has been interpreted in numerous tasty versions to recall the typical aromas of the Mediterranean.

description: -All the countries that hug the Baltic Sea bake bread using rye flour -- rye is indigenous to the region. But it is Latvia, on the eastern shore of the Baltic sea, that produces the most delicious highest quality rye bread, as evidenced by top prizes at food exhibitions and by exports to neighboring countries. -Latvian rye bread has been praised in Gourmet magazine by its former editor-in-chief Ruth Reichl: “This is powerful stuff that reminds you of why bread is called the staff of life. I am pretty sure you could live on it alone...” -One hundred percent sourdough rye bread is the traditional staple of Latvia, and it is central to Latvian culinary and cultural history. For a thousand years Latvians baked this bread in wood burning ovens reaching 1800 degrees fahrenheit, using 100 percent rye flour, sourdough starter, a hint of caraway and little else. -In Latvia babies teethe on the rye bread. On long voyages Baltic sailors fill the holds of their ships with it- sourdough rye lasts for months. Latvians soak rye bread in milk and eggs to make bread pudding. They serve rye bread croutons fried in garlic and butter as bar snacks. Like rice in Asia, rye bread -- known as rupjmaize in Latvian -- is considered holy. It is never wasted. To leave it bottom side up on the counter is considered disrespectful. -The bread itself -- dense, dark, sweet/sour with a hint of caraway -- marries perfectly with the foods of Baltic farms and fisheries: rich butter, herring, smoked meats, fish, and pork sausage. -While the rye breads of Denmark and Sweden are known as the base for those countries excellent open-faced sandwiches, Latvian rye bread, made without any wheat, is considered the ne plus ultra of rye breads. -For decades bread lovers hungering for 100 percent sour dough rye have had to air freight it from Europe at high cost.
